title: Engage vgmtrans maintainers: post initiative + both RFCs for early signoff
description: Before heavy C++ work, open a GitHub discussion/issue on vgmtrans/vgmtrans summarizing the raw-disc-input initiative and the two RFCs (multi-collection architecture; per-game on-disc compression seam). Goal: secure direction/signoff on the architectural seams that are expensive to change later, and confirm appetite for upstreaming a generic PS1 disc-image loader. Capture maintainer decisions back into the RFC issues' design fields before implementation proceeds.

title: RFC: extension point for game-dependent on-disc compression/encoding
description: On-disc sound data is often compressed/encoded per game (e.g. FF7 LZS, FF9 packing) and must be decoded BEFORE the sequence can even be located/parsed -- unlike PSF where the loader already hands the scanner a flat RAM image. vgmtrans precedent is scattered: loaders decode whole files (KabukiDecrypt, CPS3Decrypt) and some scanners decode inline (TriAcePS1); there is NO general seam for pluggable per-game disc codecs. Design that seam and get maintainer signoff. OPTIONS TO PRESENT: (A) disc loader runs a per-game codec and emits already-decompressed VirtFiles (keeps scanners clean); (B) a pluggable 'disc codec/layout provider' interface keyed by game-DB entry; (C) decode inside the scanner (matches TriAcePS1 but couples codec to format). Reference implementations to port live in this repo: psx/ff7/unlzs.pl, psx/ff7/unpack_kernel_bin.pl, psx/lod/unpack.pl. Deliverable: written design note + recommended option for maintainer feedback.

title: RFC: single game image -> multiple VGMColls (multi-song architecture)
description: vgmtrans's typical input (one PSF) = one song; a disc/ROM holds many songs. Design how one image yields N playable VGMColls and get maintainer signoff BEFORE implementation. Good news: infrastructure largely exists -- the Matcher (FilegroupMatcher/GetIdMatcher/SimpleMatcher) already groups multiple seqs+instrsets+sampcolls from one scan into multiple VGMColls, and KonamiArcadeScanner already emits many sequences from one MAME romset driven by a seq_table + per-game offsets in an XML game-DB entry (getHexAttribute). PROPOSAL TO EVALUATE: reuse that pattern for discs -- a disc loader + disc-aware scanner that reads a per-game song table and emits N collections, with per-game metadata externalized (XML game-DB, mirroring this repo's akao/*.yaml). OPEN QUESTIONS for maintainers: (1) loader vs scanner vs matcher responsibility split for disc layout; (2) how a single loaded disc surfaces many collections in the UI/Root; (3) acceptable shape of a per-game disc-definition record. Deliverable: written design note posted for maintainer feedback.

title: AKAO-from-disc path: locate blocks, feed AkaoScanner, validate FF7
description: Using the mounted disc, locate AKAO sequence/sample blocks (per-game offsets/signatures from RE) and present them to the existing AkaoScanner -- either by producing a RAM-image VirtFile or invoking the scanner at known offsets. Acceptance: extracting one game (FF7) from its original disc yields VGMSeq/MIDI byte-identical (or musically identical) to the PSF-rip path established in the bootstrap issue.
notes: EARLY SIGNAL (from environment test, pre-implementation): fed a standalone extracted Chrono Cross AKAO block (z:/psx/cc/akao/02-1d15c.bin) to the freshly-built vgmtrans-cli. RESULT: AkaoScanner correctly finds the 'AKAO' signature, guessVersion->3_2, isPossibleAkaoSeq passes, parseHeader OK (track_bits 0x7fff=15 tracks, instr ptr 0x930), and the 15 track pointers are valid/in-range (track1@0x5e, then 0x603,0x64c,...). BUT VGMSeq::load() returns false -> seq not registered -> CLI reports 'not a recognized music file'. Extraction is sound; failure is in track EVENT parsing. HYPOTHESIS: vgmtrans targets PSF RAM images (block embedded in 2MB RAM); a standalone .bin that ends exactly after the instrument section (file size 0x9c0, instr@0x930) likely makes a track event-read run past EOF. IMPLICATIONS: (1) the disc loader (8lo.3) should present blocks within a larger buffer / padded region, OR ensure end-of-track handling; (2) possible CC parity nuance (cross-ref 8lo.6). For a clean PSF->AKAO BASELINE (8lo.1), use an actual PSF rip rather than a standalone block. Build/run environment itself is fully validated.

title: PS1 disc-image FileLoader (.cue/.bin/.iso) -> VirtFiles
description: New vgmtrans FileLoader that mounts a raw PS1 CD image: parse 2352-byte raw sectors + ISO9660 directory, expose contained files (EXE, overlays, sound data) as VirtFiles for downstream scanners. Port logic from this repo's psx/*/readsectors.pl, dump_iso_dir.pl, dump_path_table.pl. This is the core input-breadth deliverable and is reusable beyond AKAO. Register via LoaderRegistration; add to CMake.

title: Survey & design: PSFLoader->AkaoScanner pipeline + disc-loader contract
description: Document exactly how PSFLoader builds the PS1 RAM image and how AkaoScanner consumes a RawFile to emit VGMSeq/VGMInstrSet. Specify the minimal contract a disc-based loader must satisfy so the EXISTING AkaoScanner fires unchanged (VirtFile shape, base addresses, where it expects sequence vs sample tables). Map where AKAO data physically lives on each disc (main EXE, overlays, or standalone sound files) for FF7/FF8/FF9/Chrono Cross, drawing on this repo's psx/*/extract_akao + findakao tools. Check whether CHDLoader already provides reusable disc mounting. Output: short design doc + in-scope game list.
design:
SURVEY & DESIGN (drafted from vgmtrans + this repo's psx/ code reading; live-build validation still pending 8lo.1)

=== 1. PSFLoader -> VirtFile pipeline ===
PSFLoader.apply(RawFile) detects 'PSF'+version, builds an Image by overlay()ing the
PSF EXE (at its EXE-header load address) plus recursive _lib/_libN files, then:
  new VirtFile(img.data, img.size, name, path, tag); enqueue(virt);
The VirtFile is just the flat EXE/RAM bytes (offset 0 = lowest load addr). Tag (incl.
album) is carried from PSF metadata.

=== 2. Root chain (Root.cpp:87-125) ===
Per RawFile: run ALL LoaderManager loaders (each may enqueue VirtFiles), then run
scanners (extension-specific if any registered for the ext, else ALL scanners).
Enqueued VirtFiles recurse through the same loader+scanner path. enqueue() is the
FileLoader hook.

=== 3. AkaoScanner.scan(RawFile) ===
- version = determineVersionFromTag(file): switch on tag.album string ("Final Fantasy 7",
  "Chrono Cross", "Final Fantasy 9", ...). UNKNOWN -> per-block guessVersion().
- Byte-scans the ENTIRE file for BE 0x414B414F ("AKAO") at every offset.
  * seq_length (readShort @ off+6) != 0  -> AkaoSeq(file, off, ver); then seq->newInstrSet()
  * seq_length == 0                       -> AkaoSampColl(file, off, ver)
  id = readShort @ off+4. Seq/SampColl parse RELATIVE to their block offset in the file.
- Hard-coded FF7 hack: if size>=0x1A8000 and words@0xe0000/0x156000==0x1010, load an
  AkaoSampColl from fixed RAM offsets (the FF7 instrAll/instrDat instrument tables).
  This is exactly the kind of per-game constant this repo externalizes to YAML.
- AkaoMatcher pairs seqs<->instrSets<->sampColls BY ID into AkaoColl (its own matcher/coll,
  not the generic FilegroupMatcher).

=== 4. KEY CONCLUSION: multi-song is ALREADY solved for AKAO ===
Because the scanner byte-scans the whole image for every "AKAO" and the matcher pairs by
id, a single RawFile holding many AKAO blocks already yields many AkaoColls with NO scanner
changes. 8lo.8 (multi-song RFC) is therefore about GENERALITY/UX (other drivers, surfacing
N colls per disc), not an AKAO mechanism gap.

=== 5. DISC-LOADER CONTRACT (minimal, for unchanged AkaoScanner) ===
A disc loader must produce a RawFile/VirtFile such that:
 (a) AKAO seq + sampcoll blocks appear as CONTIGUOUS bytes (sectors cooked, archives
     unpacked, game compression decoded) -- so the signature scan + relative parse work.
 (b) tag.album set to a recognized string (clean path) OR rely on guessVersion fallback.
 (c) enqueue() it; Root auto-runs AkaoScanner; AkaoMatcher builds the collections.
Instrument/sample data that is NOT "AKAO"-tagged (FF7 instrAll/instrDat) needs explicit
per-game pointers (today: hard-coded; target: per-game config like the YAMLs).

=== 6. CHDLoader reuse ===
Only handles CHD (magic 'MComprHD'): decompresses all hunks to one flat buffer, wraps in a
single VirtFile (propagates file->tag), enqueues. Does NOT parse a filesystem. NOT directly
reusable for raw .bin/.cue/.iso, but its pattern (decode -> one VirtFile -> enqueue ->
signature scan) is the template for the "simple/cooked-image" path. The new PS1 disc loader
(8lo.3) is a sibling loader, not a CHDLoader extension.

=== 7. WHERE AKAO LIVES PER GAME (from this repo's psx tools) ===
- Chrono Cross (psx/cc/extractakao.pl): raw 2352-byte sectors; AKAO blocks span sectors and
  MUST be cooked (strip 24-byte subheader, keep 0x800 data) to become contiguous. No archive,
  no compression -> easiest once sector-cooking exists.
- FF9 (extract_akao.pl, findakao): custom archive FF9.IMG with a typed directory (DB types
  incl. 7=Song data, 9=Instrument data), 0x800 cooked sectors. Must parse FF9.IMG dir, emit
  Song/Instrument entries. findakao confirms a plain "AKAO" byte-scan finds blocks in the
  cooked image -- i.e. vgmtrans scanner works as-is on it.
- FF7 (extract_akao.pl): AKAO embedded INSIDE field-script DAT files + world-map TXZ, located
  via per-file extraOffset tables in each file's header. Field files live in the ISO9660 FS and
  are LZS-compressed -> needs FS walk + per-file decompress (psx/ff7/unlzs.pl) + offset-table
  walk. Most complex; this is the case that motivates the compression-seam RFC (8lo.9).
- FF8: not yet surveyed here; expect FF7-class complexity (own packing). Survey before scoping.

=== 8. IMPLICATION FOR 8lo.3 (disc loader) ===
Two-tier design recommended:
  Tier 1 (cooked-image path, mirrors CHDLoader): mount .cue/.bin/.iso, cook 2352->2048
  (mode2/form1, strip subheader), produce a logical image; for CC/FF9 this is enough to
  byte-scan. Reuse logic from psx/*/readsectors.pl + dump_iso_dir/path_table.
  Tier 2 (per-game extraction): ISO9660 FS walk -> locate game-specific archives/files ->
  per-game decode (FF9.IMG dir; FF7 LZS + extraOffset tables) -> emit per-file VirtFiles.
  Tier 2 is where 8lo.9 (compression seam) and 8lo.5 (per-game config) plug in.

=== 9. IN-SCOPE GAMES (difficulty order) ===
  1. Chrono Cross   - sector-cook only (lowest risk first target)
  2. FF9            - FF9.IMG archive dir parse, cooked sectors
  3. FF7            - ISO9660 + LZS decompress + embedded offset tables (needs 8lo.9)
  4. FF8            - survey first; likely FF7-class

title: vgmtrans bootstrap: fork, build locally, confirm PSF->AKAO baseline
description: Fork vgmtrans/vgmtrans (delivery = upstream PRs). Build the project locally on this Windows/CMake setup; resolve toolchain/deps. Run it against a known FF PSF rip and confirm the existing Akao format produces correct VGMSeq/MIDI. Establishes the working baseline every later issue is validated against.
notes:
ENVIRONMENT VALIDATED (build half of bootstrap done). Toolchain: VS 2026 / MSVC 19.51 (cl 14.51) x64, cmake 3.29.2, Ninja. All git submodules already initialized (spdlog, libchdr, zlib, vgmtrans-ext-win). Deps resolved from Strawberry (liblzma, libz) + built-in unarr/zstd. Build recipe (CLI-only, fast path; shares win-x64 preset with VS Code CMake Tools): 
  cmd /c '"...VsDevCmd.bat" -startdir=none -arch=x64 -host_arch=x64 && cd /d Z:\git\vgmtrans && cmake --preset win-x64 -DENABLE_UI_QT=OFF -DENABLE_CLI=ON && cmake --build --preset win-x64-debug'
Result: configure 29s OK; build 242/242 OK; produced build/win-x64/bin/Debug/vgmtrans-cli.exe which runs (prints usage). 208 benign C4267 warnings, 0 errors. NOTE 'tee' is not a cmd builtin -- use cmd redirection (> log 2>&1) not | tee. Pre-existing stale build dirs: build/ root was a Unix-Makefiles/WSL config (ignore); build/win-x64 had an incomplete cache (was removed and re-created cleanly).
REMAINING for 8lo.1: (a) PSF->AKAO baseline conversion test (need a PSF rip to feed the CLI: vgmtrans-cli <file.psf/.minipsf> -o outdir, then verify a MIDI is produced from the AKAO seq); (b) fork the upstream repo (deferred until ready to push PRs).

title: Tier A: externalize FF7 hard-coded scanner constants -> data-driven AKAO game-DB entry
description: Replace vgmtrans's hard-coded FF7 handling with per-game DATA, mirroring the existing MAME XML game-DB pattern (KonamiArcadeScanner reads seq_table/samp_tables via getHexAttribute). Concretely externalize: (1) AkaoScanner's hard-coded AkaoInstrDatLocation(0xe0000,0x156000,0,128) + 0x1A8000/0x1010 magic; (2) determineVersionFromTag's album->version switch; (3) optional song id->title naming (today auto-named 'Akao Seq {id}'). This is the data half of this repo's ff7.yaml. IMPORTANT: externalization is REQUIRED for the disc path, not just cleanup -- on a real disc the RAM-image offsets 0xe0000/0x156000 are meaningless; you have ISO9660/archive offsets that must come from per-game data. Idiomatic and maintainer-friendly given the MAME precedent. Effort: moderate (struct + lookup + scanner refactor).
design: Decomposition of porting this repo's config-driven AKAO strategy into vgmtrans. TIER A (this issue) = externalize per-game CONSTANTS/locations into a game-DB record. Idiomatic: MAME loader already does XML game-DB (getHexAttribute). Required for disc loading (8lo.3/8lo.5) because RAM-image offsets don't exist on disc. Maps to ff7.yaml's instrument-location + version + songs fields. Keep the hand-written AkaoSeq parser (that's Tier C).

title: AKAO Seq parity gaps: diff Python opcode handling vs vgmtrans AkaoSeq
description: Compare this repo's akao/ Python opcode/event handling (ir_events.py, format_psx.py) against vgmtrans's AkaoSeq to find opcodes/variants vgmtrans mis-handles or omits (e.g. Chrono Cross specifics, volume/expression mapping). File concrete parity fixes against upstream AkaoSeq. Independent of the loader work; can proceed in parallel after the survey.
notes: FIRST CONCRETE PARITY FINDING (empirical, via vgmtrans-cli on real Chrono Cross AKAO data): vgmtrans AkaoSeq emits 'Unknown Event 0xFE 0x13' and the track parse derails. ROOT CAUSE: vgmtrans's hand-written event map lacks 0xFE13. This repo's akao/chrono_cross.yaml ALSO marks 0xFE13 semantic=unknown -- BUT with params:0, i.e. it knows the OPERAND LENGTH even without the semantic, so the Python parser skips it and continues. LESSON (the core parity-robustness pattern): for not breaking, operand LENGTHS matter more than semantics. ACTION for vgmtrans: audit AkaoSeq's FE-subcode handling against this repo's fe_opcode_table (format_psx.py fe_oplen + chrono_cross/ff8/ff9 yaml) and add missing subcodes (0xFE13 and others in 0x08-0x1F range) with correct lengths even when semantics are unknown, so unknown-but-known-length opcodes don't abort the track. This is also the strongest concrete motivation for Tier C (8lo.13): a data-driven opcode-LENGTH table is what makes parsing robust. Also seen: standalone/concatenated seq blocks produce 0 MIDI output because the CLI exports matched VGMColls (seq+sampcoll paired by id); sample-collection AKAO blocks (seq_length==0) must be present+matched -- cross-ref 8lo.4.

title: Tier B: AKAO render-strategy selection (velocity/expression/cc7) as SeqTrack/format option
description: Port this repo's midi_render.strategy concept (velocity vs expression/CC11 vs CC7 mapping of AKAO volume) into vgmtrans as a per-format/per-game render option. Maintainer precedent is fresh: vgmtrans commit 0f01dc7c added a 'linear amplitude scale at the SeqTrack level' flag, so volume-rendering options at SeqTrack level are already accepted. Upstreamable as a STANDALONE PR independent of the disc work. OPEN CHALLENGE (why this is lower priority): determining the 'right' render selection for a given driver/game is non-trivial -- needs analysis/listening comparison; the selection criteria are not yet well-defined. Lower priority per owner; do eventually.
design: TIER B of the strategy-port decomposition. Cleanly portable concept; rides existing SeqTrack volume-flag precedent (commit 0f01dc7c). Hard part is not the mechanism but choosing correct strategy per game -- defer until selection criteria are characterized (feeds from 8lo.6 parity analysis).

title: Tier C: data-driven AKAO opcode interpreter (merge config-driven + hand-written parser)
description: EVENTUAL, MAINTAINER-GATED. Explore merging this repo's data-driven opcode-table approach with vgmtrans's hand-written ~1600-line AkaoSeq parser. Owner sees this as a merging of techniques, not a wholesale replacement -- but it is a MAJOR refactor that diverges from how every other vgmtrans format works (all formats use hand-coded Seq classes), so it REQUIRES upfront discussion/signoff with maintainers before any code. Until then, this repo's opcode YAML is used only as a reference spec to fix parity bugs (see 8lo.6), not as runtime config. Deliverable: a written proposal/RFC framing the merge and its tradeoffs for maintainer discussion.
design: TIER C of the strategy-port decomposition. NOT recommended as a wholesale port (would replace a working 1598-line parser; divergent from vgmtrans norms => likely 'no'). Owner frames it as merging techniques + major refactor needing maintainer discussion first. Gate behind maintainer engagement (8lo.10). Reference-only use of opcode YAML in the meantime via 8lo.6.
